tools.name: analytics_getAllLatestHistoryData
tools.title: Latest Analytics Values
tools.description:
Retrieves the most recent value(s) of a specific technical indicator or financial metric 
            for a cryptocurrency from the altFINS platform.

            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - The latest data point(s) for a single indicator and single symbol
            - Each record contains a timestamp and the indicator value at that point
            - Returns the most current available value for the requested analyticsType

            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks "what is the current RSI for BTC?"
            - User wants to validate a single indicator value before making a decision
            - You need the most recent value of an indicator to construct or confirm a technical analysis
            - User asks "what is ETH's current market cap?"
            - User asks "what is the latest MACD value for SOL?"
            - You are building a technical analysis and need to verify current indicator values

            ### DO NOT USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
            - User wants HISTORICAL data over a time range → use getHistoryAnalyticsData instead
            - User wants to SCREEN or FILTER multiple coins → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData instead
            - User wants OHLCV price candles → use ohlc_getLatestData instead
            - User wants to compare an indicator across many coins simultaneously → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData

            ### DIFFERENCE FROM getHistoryAnalyticsData:
            - This tool → returns the LATEST/CURRENT value only (no date range needed)
            - getHistoryAnalyticsData → returns a time-series of HISTORICAL values over a date range

            ### COMBINE WITH OTHER TOOLS:
            - Use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData to find interesting coins first,
              then call this tool to get the exact current indicator value for confirmation
            - Combine multiple calls (one per analyticsType) to build a complete 
              current technical picture for a single coin

            ### IMPORTANT:
            - One call returns data for ONE symbol and ONE analyticsType only
            - To get multiple indicators for the same coin, make separate calls per analyticsType

tools.name: analytics_getAnalyticsTypes
tools.title: Analytics Types
tools.description:
Returns the complete list of available analytics types from the altFINS platform.
            Each entry includes a machine-readable identifier and a human-friendly display name.

            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - A list of all valid analyticsType values accepted by the getHistoryAnalyticsData tool
            - Each item contains:
            - identifier   → the exact string value to pass as 'analyticsType' parameter
            - displayName  → human-readable label (e.g. "RSI 14", "SMA 50", "Market Cap")

            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks "what indicators are available?" or "what metrics can I track?"
            - User asks "what analytics types does altFINS support?"
            - You are unsure whether a specific analyticsType value is valid before calling 
              getHistoryAnalyticsData — use this tool to verify first
            - User wants to browse or explore available metrics before choosing one

            ### DO NOT USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
            - You already know the analyticsType value the user needs (e.g. RSI14, MACD, SMA50)
              → call getHistoryAnalyticsData directly without discovery step
            - User wants actual historical data → use getHistoryAnalyticsData instead
            - User wants current indicator values → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData instead

            ### RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER TOOLS:
            - This is a DISCOVERY tool for getHistoryAnalyticsData
            - The identifier values returned here are the exact valid inputs for the 
              'analyticsType' parameter in getHistoryAnalyticsData
            - Call this tool once if needed, then use the identifier in subsequent calls

            ### IMPORTANT:
            - This tool takes no parameters and requires no input
            - Results are static — the list of analytics types does not change between calls
            - No need to call this tool repeatedly in the same session

tools.name: analytics_getHistoryData
tools.title: Analytics History
tools.description:
Retrieves historical time-series data for technical indicators and financial metrics 
            for a specific cryptocurrency over a given time range.

            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - A time-ordered list of historical values for a single indicator (e.g. RSI14 values over last 30 days)
            - Each record contains a timestamp and the indicator value at that point in time
            - Supports all major technicals: SMA, EMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, Volume, Market Cap, Revenue, TVL, and more
    
            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks "how has RSI changed over the last 30 days for BTC?"
            - User wants to see the historical trend of an indicator, not just its current value
            - User asks "show me ETH market cap history for this year"
            - User wants to chart or analyze how a metric evolved over time
            - User asks "was SOL overbought last month?" (requires historical RSI data)
            - User wants to compare indicator values across different time periods
    
            ### DO NOT USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
            - User wants the CURRENT value of an indicator → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData instead
            - User wants to SCREEN or FILTER multiple coins by an indicator → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
            - User wants OHLCV price history → use ohlc_getHistoryData instead
            - User wants the latest single value → use analytics_getAllLatestHistoryData instead
    
            ### COMBINE WITH OTHER TOOLS:
            - Use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData first to identify interesting coins, 
              then call this tool to get the historical indicator trend for a specific coin
            - Combine with ohlc_getHistoryData to correlate price action with indicator history
            
            ### IMPORTANT:
            - This tool returns data for ONE symbol and ONE analyticsType per call
            - To compare multiple indicators, make separate calls for each analyticsType
            - Always specify a meaningful time range — without from/to the results may be limited

from.description:
Start of the time range (inclusive) for historical data retrieval.
            
                ### ACCEPTED FORMATS:
                - ISO 8601: 2025-10-28T00:00:00.000
                - Natural language: 'today', 'yesterday', 'this week', 'this month', 'this year',
                  'last 7 days', 'last 30 days', 'last 90 days', 'last 12 months',
                  'last week', 'last month', 'last year'
                
                ### COMMON USE CASES:
                - "last 30 days of RSI"  → from='last 30 days'
                - "RSI this year"        → from='this year'
                - "last week's MACD"     → from='last week'
                
                💡 TIP: Always pair with 'to' parameter to define a complete range.
                💡 TIP: For 'last X days' queries, set from='last X days' and omit 'to' (defaults to now).

to.description:
End of the time range (inclusive) for historical data retrieval.
            
                ### ACCEPTED FORMATS:
                - ISO 8601: 2025-10-28T00:00:00.000
                - Natural language: 'today', 'yesterday', 'this week', 'this month', 'this year',
                  'last 7 days', 'last 30 days', 'last 90 days', 'last 12 months',
                  'last week', 'last month', 'last year'
                
                💡 TIP: If the user asks for data "up to now" or "until today", set to='today'.
                💡 TIP: Can be omitted when using natural language in 'from' — end of range is derived automatically.

page.description: Page number for pagination, zero-based index. Default is 0 (first page).

size.description:
Number of records per page. Default is 10. Maximum is 1000.
            
                ### SELECTION GUIDE:
                - Quick overview (last few values)  → 10–20
                - Weekly analysis (DAILY interval)  → 7
                - Monthly analysis (DAILY interval) → 30
                - Yearly analysis (DAILY interval)  → 365
                - Intraday analysis (HOURLY)        → 24–48
                - Full history export               → 1000 (use sparingly)
                
                ⚠️ Requesting more than 1000 will return an error.

sortField.description:

                ### ALLOWED VALUES:
                - timestamp → sort by date/time of the data point (default, recommended)
                - time      → same as timestamp (the name of the response field)
                - value     → sort by the indicator value (useful for finding min/max periods)
            
                ⚠️ Only these values are accepted; any other value is rejected.

sortDirection.description:
Sort order direction.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES:
                - ASC  → ascending, oldest data first (use for charting/plotting over time)
                - DESC → descending, most recent data first (default, use for "latest values")
            
                💡 TIP: Use ASC when you need data in chronological order for trend analysis or charting.
                💡 TIP: Use DESC (default) when the user wants the most recent values first.

tools.name: getCryptoCalendarEvents
tools.title: Crypto Calendar Events
tools.description:
Search and filter cryptocurrency calendar events such as AMAs, exchange listings, 
            airdrops, partnerships, protocol releases, and conferences.
            
            ### CORE CAPABILITIES:
            - Filter by asset symbol, event category, date ranges, keywords, and vote rankings
            - Supports pagination and sorting for large result sets

            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks about "upcoming events" for a coin or the market
            - User asks about "catalysts", "news events", "airdrops", "listings", or "conferences"
            - User wants to combine technical analysis with fundamental event context
            - User asks "what's happening with [coin] this week/month\"
            
            ### BEST FOR:
            "Show me upcoming Solana events this week", "Any airdrops coming soon?",
            "What conferences are happening this month?", "Show hot events for BTC and ETH"
            
            ### NO RESULTS:
            - Strict filters often match nothing; relaxed filters (no titleKeyword, a wider date
              range) usually find events.

quickSearch.description:
Full-text search term matched across all event data fields (title, description, asset name).
                Use for broad keyword searches when you don't know the exact field to search.
            
                Examples: "Binance listing", "mainnet launch", "token burn"

Filter events by their RELEASE DATE (the date the event was published/announced).
                This is NOT the date the event takes place — use eventFrom/eventTo for that.
                
                Defines the START of the release date range (inclusive).
                
                ### ACCEPTED FORMATS:
                - ISO 8601: 2025-10-28T00:00:00.000
                - Natural language: 'today', 'yesterday', 'this week', 'this month', 'this year',
                  'last 7 days', 'last 30 days', 'last 90 days', 'last 12 months',
                  'last week', 'last month', 'last year'
                
                💡 TIP: Always pair with releaseTo to define a complete range.
                ⚠️ Do NOT use this to filter when an event happens — use eventFrom instead.

Filter events marked as HOT by community voting.
                Hot events have high immediate engagement and attention.
                
                Set to true to include only hot events.
                
                💡 TIP: Combine voteIsHot=true + voteIsTrending=true to find the most 
                socially active events right now.

voteIsTrending.description:
Filter events marked as TRENDING by community voting.
                Trending events are gaining momentum in community interest.
                
                Set to true to include only trending events.
                
                💡 TIP: Combine voteIsTrending=true + voteIsSignificant=true to find 
                events that are both gaining traction and considered important.

voteIsSignificant.description:
Filter events marked as SIGNIFICANT by community voting.
                Significant events are considered high-impact or important by the community.
                
                Set to true to include only significant events.
                
                💡 TIP: Use voteIsSignificant=true when the user asks for "important events", 
                "major catalysts", or "high impact news".

category.description:
Filter events by category type.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES (use exact values, case-sensitive):
                RELEASE, BRANDING, TOKENOMICS, EXCHANGE, CONFERENCE, COMMUNITY,
                OTHER, AIRDROP, AMA, PARTNERSHIP, ROADMAP_UPDATE, FORK_SWAP,
                WHITEPAPER_UPDATE, DEV_UPDATE
                
                ### FORMAT:
                - Single category: AIRDROP
                - Multiple categories: RELEASE,EXCHANGE,AIRDROP (comma-separated, no spaces)
                
                ### CATEGORY GUIDE — map user intent to correct value:
                - "listing" or "exchange listing"   → EXCHANGE
                - "airdrop" or "token drop"         → AIRDROP
                - "AMA" or "ask me anything"         → AMA
                - "conference" or "summit"           → CONFERENCE
                - "partnership" or "collaboration"   → PARTNERSHIP
                - "roadmap" or "milestone update"    → ROADMAP_UPDATE
                - "fork" or "swap" or "migration"    → FORK_SWAP
                - "whitepaper"                       → WHITEPAPER_UPDATE
                - "tokenomics" or "token burn"       → TOKENOMICS
                - "dev update" or "developer update" → DEV_UPDATE
                - "release" or "launch" or "mainnet" → RELEASE
                - "rebranding" or "brand change"     → BRANDING
                - "community" or "social"            → COMMUNITY
                
                ⚠️ Do NOT send values outside this list — unknown values will be rejected.

descriptionKeyword.description:
Filter events whose DESCRIPTION contains this keyword (case-insensitive, partial match).
                Use when the user wants to search inside event details, not just the title.
                
                Examples: "Binance", "staking rewards", "v2 upgrade"
                
                💡 TIP: Use quickSearch for broader matching across all fields, 
                use descriptionKeyword only when the user specifically refers to event content/details.

page.description: Page number for pagination, zero-based index. Default is 0 (first page).

size.description: Number of records per page. Default is 10. Maximum recommended is 50.

sortField.description:
Field to sort results by.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES (use exact values, case-sensitive):
                - dateEvent   → sort by the date the event takes place
                - createdDate → sort by the date the event was published (default)
                
                ⚠️ Only these two values are accepted. Any other value will be ignored or cause an error.

sortDirection.description:
Sort order direction.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES:
                - ASC  → ascending (oldest first)
                - DESC → descending (newest first, default)

tools.name: news_getCryptoNewsMessages
tools.title: Crypto News
tools.description:
Search and filter cryptocurrency news articles and messages from multiple 
            crypto news sources, with support for time ranges, asset filtering,
            and keyword search.

            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - A list of news message summaries matching the filters
            - Each result includes the title, text, link to the original article, source, timestamp,
              and related asset symbols
            - The items are written by third-party news sites and X accounts; altFINS collects them
              but does not write or edit them
            - Results are sorted by timestamp (newest first) by default

            ### TYPICAL USES:
            - Latest news for a coin or for the crypto market
            - "What's happening with BTC/ETH/SOL?"
            - News context for a technical analysis
            - News about a coin within a time range, such as this week
            - What is being reported about a crypto topic
            - News from a specific news source

            ### NOT COVERED BY THIS TOOL:
            - Upcoming scheduled events (AMAs, listings, conferences): getCryptoCalendarEvents
            - Technical analysis or price data: screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
            - Social sentiment scores

            ### RELATED TOOLS:
            - screener_getAltfinsScreenerData finds technically interesting coins; this tool adds
              recent news context for them
            - getCryptoCalendarEvents adds upcoming events to the news for a fuller fundamental picture
            - news_getCryptoNewsSources lists the exact source names accepted by 'sources'
            - getUserPortfolio returns the coins the user holds; their tickers in
              assetSymbolsKeywords give news about the user's portfolio

            ### FILTERS:
            - Broad topic: quickSearch with a topic keyword
            - Specific coins: assetSymbolsKeywords with the coin tickers
            - Headline or article wording: titleKeyword or contentKeyword
            - All filters that are set must match (AND logic)

quickSearch.description:
Search term matched against the news text and the related asset symbols
                (case-insensitive, partial match).
                Suits broad topic searches that do not target one specific field.
            
                ### EXAMPLES:
                - "Bitcoin ETF"
                - "Ethereum upgrade"
                - "SEC regulation"
                - "DeFi hack"

                💡 TIP: titleKeyword matches the headline only; contentKeyword matches the headline
                or the article text. quickSearch does not match the headline.
                💡 TIP: Combined with titleKeyword or contentKeyword, every search term that is set
                must match.

from.description:
Start of the news time range (inclusive). Filters news published at or after this time.

                ### ACCEPTED FORMATS:
                - ISO-8601 UTC: 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z
                - Natural language: 'today', 'yesterday', 'this week', 'this month', 'this year',
                  'last 7 days', 'last 30 days', 'last 90 days', 'last 12 months',
                  'last week', 'last month', 'last year'

                💡 TIP: A natural-language value sets both ends of the range, and 'to' is not used.
                With an ISO-8601 value, 'to' sets the end; without 'to' the range is open-ended.
                💡 TIP: from='today' or from='last 7 days' covers "latest news".
                ⚠️ Natural-language values are matched as whole phrases, including the spaces.

to.description:
End of the news time range (inclusive), as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp,
                for example 2025-11-03T00:00:00Z. Filters news published at or before this time.

                💡 TIP: Not used when 'from' is a natural-language value, which sets both ends.
                💡 TIP: Without 'to', the range runs up to now.

assetSymbolsKeywords.description:
Filter news by one or more cryptocurrency asset symbols.
                Returns only news articles related to the specified coins.
            
                ### FORMAT:
                - Single symbol:   BTC
                - Multiple symbols: BTC,ETH,SOL (comma-separated, no spaces)
                
                ### EXAMPLES:
                - User asks "BTC news"          → assetSymbolsKeywords=BTC
                - User asks "news for BTC, ETH" → assetSymbolsKeywords=BTC,ETH
                - User asks "Solana news"       → assetSymbolsKeywords=SOL

                ⚠️ Values are coin ticker symbols (BTC, not Bitcoin; ETH, not Ethereum).
                ⚠️ Trading pairs such as BTCUSDT match nothing.

sources.description:
Filter news by one or more news source names.
                Returns only articles from the specified sources.

                ### FORMAT:
                - Single source:    one source name
                - Multiple sources: comma-separated source names

                💡 TIP: news_getCryptoNewsSources lists the exact source names.
                ⚠️ Names are matched exactly, ignoring case. If any name matches no source, the
                request fails with an error that lists the unknown names; it is never widened to
                all sources.

titleKeyword.description:
Filter news whose TITLE contains this keyword (case-insensitive, partial match).
                Suits requests for articles with a specific topic in the headline.
            
                ### EXAMPLES:
                - "ETF approval"
                - "hack"
                - "upgrade"
                - "partnership"
                
                💡 TIP: titleKeyword suits requests about article headlines.
                💡 TIP: contentKeyword matches the headline or the article text.
                💡 TIP: quickSearch matches the article text or the related asset symbols.

contentKeyword.description:
Filter news whose headline OR article text contains this keyword (case-insensitive,
                partial match). Suits requests for articles that mention something anywhere in the
                article, not only in the headline.

                ### EXAMPLES:
                - "Binance listing"
                - "staking rewards"
                - "regulatory approval"

                💡 TIP: titleKeyword matches the headline only.
                💡 TIP: quickSearch matches the article text or the related asset symbols, but not
                the headline.

page.description: Page number for pagination, zero-based index. Default is 0 (first page).

size.description:
Number of news articles per page. Default is 10. Values above 1000 are capped at 1000.

                💡 TIP: 10-20 articles suit a normal news question; each article carries its text,
                so pages above 50 produce very long responses.

sortField.description:
Field to sort news results by.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES:
                - timestamp    → sort by publication date/time (default)
                - assetSymbols → sort alphabetically by related coin symbols
                - title        → sort alphabetically by article title
                - content      → sort alphabetically by article content

                ### SELECTION GUIDE:
                - "latest news first"           → timestamp + sortDirection=DESC (default)
                - "oldest news first"           → timestamp + sortDirection=ASC
                - "news grouped by coin"        → assetSymbols

                ⚠️ Any other value is rejected with an error that lists these four values.

sortDirection.description:
Sort order direction.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES:
                - ASC  → ascending, oldest articles first
                - DESC → descending, newest articles first (default)

                💡 TIP: ASC suits requests for chronological order.

tools.name: news_getCryptoNewsSources
tools.title: Crypto News Sources
tools.description:
Lists the crypto news sources that altFINS aggregates. Each entry has an id and a name.
            Optionally narrows the list to sources whose name contains a search term.

            ### TYPICAL USES:
            - "Which crypto news sources does altFINS cover?"
            - Finding the exact name of a source for the 'sources' parameter of news_getCryptoNewsMessages

            ### NOTES:
            - The 'sources' parameter of news_getCryptoNewsMessages accepts exactly these names and rejects other names
            - This tool returns source names only; news_getCryptoNewsMessages returns the articles
            - The list changes rarely

quickSearch.description:
Optional search term that narrows the list to sources whose name contains it
                (case-insensitive; spaces are ignored). Omit quickSearch to get all news sources.

                ### EXAMPLES:
                - quickSearch="news" → every source whose name contains "news"
                - quickSearch omitted → the full list

tools.name: ohlc_getHistoryData
tools.title: OHLC Price History
tools.description:
Fetches historical OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) price candle data 
            for a specific cryptocurrency symbol over a given time range and interval.

            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - A list of OHLCV candles for the requested symbol and time range
            - Each candle contains: timestamp, open, high, low, close, volume
            - Results represent raw price action data — the building blocks of all technical analysis
    
            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks for historical price data or candlestick data for a coin
            - User asks "what was BTC's price last month?"
            - User asks "show me ETH candles for the last 30 days"
            - You need raw OHLCV data to perform or validate manual technical analysis calculations
            - User wants to analyze price action patterns over a specific period
            - User asks "what was the highest price SOL reached last week?"
    
            ### DO NOT USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
            - User wants CURRENT price or latest candle only → use ohlc_getLatestData instead
            - User wants pre-calculated technical indicators (RSI, MACD, SMA) 
              → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData or getHistoryAnalyticsData instead
            - User wants to SCREEN or FILTER multiple coins → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
            - User wants fundamental data (revenue, TVL) → use getHistoryAnalyticsData instead
    
            ### COMBINE WITH OTHER TOOLS:
            - Combine with getHistoryAnalyticsData to correlate raw price candles 
              with indicator history (e.g. overlay RSI on price chart data)
            - Use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData first to identify interesting coins,
              then call this tool to get their detailed price history
    
            ### IMPORTANT:
            - Both 'from' and 'to' are required — always provide a time range
            - One call returns data for ONE symbol only
            - Use the 'size' parameter to control how many candles are returned
            - Default is 10 candles — increase size for longer time range analysis

symbol.description:
Uppercase cryptocurrency symbol to retrieve OHLCV candle data for.
            
                ### FORMAT:
                - Single symbol, uppercase only (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL, ADA)
                
                ⚠️ Use uppercase ticker symbols only.
                ⚠️ Do not use full names (e.g. use BTC not Bitcoin).
                ⚠️ Do not use trading pairs (e.g. use ETH not ETHUSDT).

timeInterval.description:
Time interval for each OHLCV candle (the granularity of price data).
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES:
                - MINUTES15 → 15-minute candles (intraday scalping, short-term)
                - HOURLY    → 1-hour candles (intraday analysis)
                - HOURS4    → 4-hour candles (swing trading)
                - HOURS12   → 12-hour candles (medium-term overview)
                - DAILY     → daily candles (default, recommended for most use cases)
                
                ### SELECTION GUIDE:
                - "today's price action" or "intraday"     → HOURLY or MINUTES15
                - "last few days" or "swing trading"       → HOURS4
                - "last month" or "standard analysis"      → DAILY
                - "last year" or "long-term price history" → DAILY
                
                ⚠️ Only these exact values are accepted. Default is DAILY.

from.description:
Start of the time range for OHLCV data (inclusive). Required.
            
                ### ACCEPTED FORMATS:
                - ISO 8601: 2025-10-28T00:00:00Z
                - Natural language: 'today', 'yesterday', 'this week', 'this month', 'this year',
                  'last 7 days', 'last 30 days', 'last 90 days', 'last 12 months',
                  'last week', 'last month', 'last year'
                
                ### COMMON USE CASES:
                - "last 30 days of candles"  → from='last 30 days', to='today'
                - "price history this year"  → from='this year', to='today'
                - "last week's candles"      → from='last week', to='today'
                
                💡 TIP: Always pair with 'to' — both are required for this tool.
                ⚠️ This parameter is required — never omit it.

to.description:
End of the time range for OHLCV data (inclusive). Required.
            
                ### ACCEPTED FORMATS:
                - ISO 8601: 2025-10-28T00:00:00Z
                - Natural language: 'today', 'yesterday', 'this week', 'this month', 'this year',
                  'last 7 days', 'last 30 days', 'last 90 days', 'last 12 months',
                  'last week', 'last month', 'last year'
                
                💡 TIP: For "up to now" or "until today", set to='today'.
                💡 TIP: Can be derived automatically when using natural language in 'from'.
                ⚠️ This parameter is required — never omit it.

page.description: Page number for pagination, zero-based index. Default is 0 (first page).

size.description:
Number of OHLCV candles per page. Default is 10. Maximum recommended is 1000.
            
                ### SELECTION GUIDE:
                - Last 7 daily candles    → size=7
                - Last 30 daily candles   → size=30
                - Last 90 daily candles   → size=90
                - Last 365 daily candles  → size=365
                - Last 24 hourly candles  → size=24
                - Last 96 x 4h candles    → size=96
                
                💡 TIP: Match size to your time range and interval combination.
                💡 TIP: For "last month" with DAILY interval, use size=30.
                💡 TIP: For "last week" with HOURLY interval, use size=168 (7 × 24).

sortField.description:
Field to sort the OHLCV candles by.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES (use exact values, case-sensitive):
                - time   → sort by candle timestamp (default, recommended)
                - open   → sort by opening price
                - high   → sort by highest price in candle
                - low    → sort by lowest price in candle
                - close  → sort by closing price
                - volume → sort by trading volume
                
                ### SELECTION GUIDE:
                - "chronological candles"         → time + sortDirection=ASC
                - "most recent candles first"     → time + sortDirection=DESC (default)
                - "highest volume candles"        → volume + sortDirection=DESC
                - "biggest price range candles"   → high + sortDirection=DESC
                
                ⚠️ Only these exact values are accepted. Any other value will be ignored.

sortDirection.description:
Sort order direction.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES:
                - ASC  → ascending, oldest candles first (use for charting/time-series analysis)
                - DESC → descending, most recent candles first (default)
                
                💡 TIP: Use ASC when you need candles in chronological order for charting or 
                sequential price analysis.
                💡 TIP: Use DESC (default) when you want the most recent price action first.

tools.name: ohlc_getLatestData
tools.title: Latest OHLC Prices
tools.description:
Fetches the latest OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) price candle(s) 
            for one or more cryptocurrency symbols at a specified time interval.
            Returns the most recent available candle data — not historical time series.
    
            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - The latest OHLCV candle for each requested symbol
            - Each record contains: symbol, timestamp, open, high, low, close, volume
            - Reflects the most current price action snapshot available
    
            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks "what is the current price of BTC?"
            - User asks "show me the latest candle for ETH"
            - User wants a quick price snapshot for one or more coins
            - User asks "what's the current volume for SOL?"
            - User wants to check current price action before making a decision
            - You need current OHLCV data to validate or enrich a technical analysis
            - User asks for price data on multiple coins simultaneously
    
            ### DO NOT USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
            - User wants HISTORICAL candles over a time range 
              → use ohlc_getHistoryData instead
            - User wants pre-calculated technical indicators (RSI, MACD, SMA) 
              → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData instead
            - User wants fundamental data (revenue, TVL, market cap) 
              → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData or getHistoryAnalyticsData instead
    
            ### DIFFERENCE FROM ohlc_getHistoryData:
            - This tool   → returns the LATEST/CURRENT candle only (no date range needed)
            - getHistoryData → returns a TIME-SERIES of historical candles over a date range
    
            ### COMBINE WITH OTHER TOOLS:
            - Use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData first to identify interesting coins,
              then call this tool to get their current OHLCV snapshot
            - Combine with getHistoryAnalyticsData to enrich current price data 
              with the latest indicator values
    
            ### IMPORTANT:
            - Provide at least one symbol — this parameter is required
            - Multiple symbols can be queried in a single call (comma-separated)
            - Returns one candle per symbol per call

symbols.description:
One or more cryptocurrency symbols to query, comma separated values for more cryptocurrency symbols (e.g., BTC, ETH), 
        only one symbol for one cryptocurrency symbol (e.g., BTC).

timeInterval.description:
Time interval of screener values. Default time interval is DAILY. 
        Only these values are allowed: MINUTES15, HOURLY, HOURS4, HOURS12, DAILY"

tools.name: symbols_getAvailableSymbols
tools.title: Available Symbols
tools.description:
Retrieves the list of cryptocurrency symbols (coin ids) available on the altFINS platform,
            optionally together with the smart contract address of each symbol on every blockchain it is deployed on.

            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - 'name' — the exact symbol to pass to the 'symbol' parameter of the other tools (e.g. "ETH")
            - 'friendlyName' — the display name of the coin (e.g. "Ethereum")
            - 'platforms' — contract addresses keyed by the blockchain (asset platform) name, for example
              {"ethereum": "0xb9ef770b6a5e12e45983c5d80545258aa38f3b78",
               "polygon-pos": "0x8bb30e0e67b11b978a5040144c410e1ccddcba30"}
              Possible platform keys: 'ethereum', 'binance-smart-chain', 'polygon-pos', 'fantom',
              'arbitrum-one', 'avalanche'. The object is EMPTY when altFINS knows no contract address for
              the symbol — native coins such as BTC and coins that are not ERC20-style tokens have no
              contract address at all.

            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks "which coins/symbols does altFINS support?"
            - User asks for the contract address of a coin, or on which chains a coin is deployed
            - User gives a coin by its full name ("Ethereum", "solana") and you need the exact symbol
              before calling another tool
            - A previous tool call returned empty and you want to verify the symbol actually exists

            ### DO NOT USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
            - You already know the exact symbol → call the data tool directly
            - User wants prices, indicators or patterns → use ohlc_*, analytics_* or screener_* tools

            ### PARAMETERS:
            - Use 'quickSearch' to narrow the result down — the full list contains thousands of symbols
            - Set 'includePlatforms' to false when you only need the symbol names; it makes the call
              cheaper and the response much smaller

            ### IMPORTANT:
            - Results are relatively static — the symbol list does not change frequently,
              there is no need to call this tool repeatedly in the same session
            - Contract addresses are returned in the lower-case form stored by altFINS

quickSearch.description:
Optional search term filtering the symbols by symbol or by friendly name
                (case-insensitive, partial match).

                ### WHEN TO USE:
                - Leave null to retrieve ALL available symbols (large response)
                - Provide a partial symbol or coin name to find a specific coin

                ### RESULT LIMITS:
                At most 2000 symbols are returned in one call, or 200 when includePlatforms is true,
                because contract addresses add an entry per blockchain per asset. A search matching
                more than that is rejected with a message saying so — narrow the term, or set
                includePlatforms=false to get the names alone.

                ### EXAMPLES:
                - quickSearch="eth"      → matches ETH/Ethereum, ETHW, WETH, ...
                - quickSearch="bitcoin"  → matches BTC (friendly name "Bitcoin")
                - quickSearch=null       → returns the full symbol list

                💡 TIP: Prefer a short partial term to maximize matches.

includePlatforms.description:
Whether the contract addresses per blockchain should be returned in the 'platforms' field.
                Defaults to true when not provided.

                ### WHEN TO USE:
                - true (or omitted) — the user asks about contract addresses, chains, or token deployments
                - false — you only need the symbol names, e.g. to validate a symbol before another tool call.
                  This skips the contract address lookup and returns a much smaller response.

tools.name: screener_getPresetFilterTypes
tools.title: Screener Preset Filters
tools.description:
Fetches all available preset filter ids (pre-built screener strategies) supported by
            the altFINS crypto screener. Each preset encodes a complete filter recipe that can be
            run with screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataByPresetFilter.

            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - A list of every valid preset filter id
            - Each entry includes:
              - id                  → the exact string to pass as 'presetFilterType' in
                                      screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataByPresetFilter
              - friendlyName        → human-readable label derived from the id
              - category            → the id prefix (SR, SB, TCP, CP1, CP2, CP3, TM, OSC, DIV, FUND, CAT)
              - categoryDescription → what that category covers
            - Examples: SR_RESISTANCE_BREAKOUT, SB_OVERSOLD_UPTREND, TM_MA_RIBBON, CAT_DEFI

            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - BEFORE the first call to screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataByPresetFilter in a session
            - User asks "what screener strategies / presets / setups are available?"
            - You are about to choose a 'presetFilterType' and are not certain of the exact id
            - A previous screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataByPresetFilter call was rejected with an
              unknown preset id → call this tool and pick the correct id, do not guess again

            ### DO NOT USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
            - You already have the exact preset id from an earlier call in this session
              → call screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataByPresetFilter directly
            - User wants actual coin data
              → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataByPresetFilter or screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
            - User wants screener display/filter metrics (RSI14, MARKET_CAP, …)
              → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataTypes instead (different set of values)

            ### RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER TOOLS:
            - This is a DISCOVERY tool for screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataByPresetFilter
            - The ids returned here are the ONLY valid values for its 'presetFilterType' parameter
            - Preset ids CANNOT be constructed by hand from the naming convention — they must
              come from this tool
            - Typical workflow: call this tool once, pick the id matching the user's intent,
              then call screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataByPresetFilter with it

            ### DIFFERENCE FROM screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataTypes:
            - This tool          → preset STRATEGY ids for the preset filter tool
            - getScreenerDataTypes → METRIC ids for displayTypes / numericFilters
            - These are DIFFERENT sets — do not mix them across tools

            ### IMPORTANT:
            - This tool takes no input — results are the same regardless of caller
            - Results are static — the preset list does not change between calls
            - No need to call this tool repeatedly in the same session

tools.name: screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
tools.title: Crypto Screener
tools.description:
Primary crypto screening engine with technical and fundamental filters (AND logic).
            Use for RSI/MACD/SMA queries, price patterns, category screens, and financial metrics.
            FALLBACK: If technicalAnalysis_getTechnicalAnalysisData returns empty, call THIS tool with that symbol.
            Call screener_getAltfinsScreenerDataTypes to discover all valid displayType and numericFilterType values.
            DO NOT use LAST_PRICE, CURRENT_PRICE, or MACD_HISTOGRAM as displayTypes.
            Best practices: technical analysis → [RSI14, MACD, SHORT_TERM_TREND, SMA50]; ATH queries → [ATH, ATH_PERCENT_DOWN, ATH_DATE].

symbols.description: Coin symbols to filter, e.g. ["BTC","ETH"]. Omit or empty list for all symbols.

timeInterval.description: Time interval of screener values. Default time interval is DAILY. Only these values are allowed: MINUTES15, HOURLY, HOURS4, HOURS12, DAILY

displayTypes.description:
Metrics to return in additionalData. Pass ONLY parent enum keys (UPPERCASE_UNDERSCORE).
           Composite metrics return NESTED objects in the response — never pass the inner leaf keys back as displayTypes:
             - SUPPORT      → {SUPPORT_1 ... SUPPORT_6}          pass "SUPPORT", not "SUPPORT_1"
             - RESISTANCE   → {RESISTANCE_1 ... RESISTANCE_6}    pass "RESISTANCE", not "RESISTANCE_1"
             - MACD         → {line, signal, histogram}              pass "MACD", not "MACD_HISTOGRAM" or "MACD_HISTOGRAM_TREND"
          SUPPORT/RESISTANCE values are chart-aligned key levels: up to 3 newest calculated S&R levels plus up to 3 nearby
          ATH/HIGH_52W/LOW_52W levels when within range of last price. ATH and HIGH_52W default to resistance; LOW_52W
          defaults to support. Recent closes can reclassify those defaults only when all required closes are on the other side.

        trading strategy or technical setup (e.g. "resistance breakouts", "oversold
        RSI in an uptrend", "bullish MACD crossover", "approaching support", "new
        1-month high", "DeFi tokens with growing TVL") and does not want to assemble
        the underlying numeric / signal / pattern filters by hand.

        ### REQUIRED FIRST STEP:
        'presetFilterType' must be an EXACT preset id. Call screener_getPresetFilterTypes
        first to get the full list of valid ids — do NOT guess an id from the naming
        convention, and do NOT invent one. An unknown id is rejected.

        ### RELATED TOOLS:

        - screener_getAltfinsScreenerData → use for fully custom multi-filter queries
          (numericFilters, signalFilters, crossAnalyticFilters, …) when no preset matches

        sort is MARKET_CAP descending.

presetFilterType.description:

        pre-built filter recipe; pick the one that matches the user's intent.

        MUST be one of the 160+ exact ids returned by screener_getPresetFilterTypes.
        Call that tool first and copy an id verbatim. The prefix legend below only tells
        you WHICH category to look in — it is NOT a recipe for constructing ids, and ids
        assembled by hand from it will be rejected.

        Naming convention (prefix → category):
        SR_*   Support / Resistance levels (breakouts, approaches, trend-filtered variants)
        SB_*   Setups & signals (pullbacks, momentum, new highs/lows, near-ATH)
        TCP_*  Technical chart patterns (triangles, channels, H&S, wedges, flags…)

        FUND_* On-chain fundamentals (TVL, revenue, MCap ratios)
        CAT_*  Market-segment categories (DeFi, Gaming, Metaverse, Stablecoins, NFTs, Memes)

tools.description:
Fetches all available value types (field identifiers) supported by the altFINS 
            crypto screener. Each value type represents a metric that can be used as a 
            display column or filter criterion in screener_getAltfinsScreenerData.
    
            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - A list of all valid screener value type identifiers
            - Each entry includes:
              - identifier  → the exact string to use in 'displayTypes' or 'numericFilters' 
                              in screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
              - displayName → human-readable label (e.g. "RSI 14", "Market Cap", "SMA 50")
            - Examples: RSI14, MACD, SMA50, MARKET_CAP, VOLUME, PRICE_CHANGE_1D
    
            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks "what fields or metrics are available in the screener?"
            - User asks "what can I filter or display in altFINS screener?"
            - You are unsure whether a specific displayType or numericFilter value is valid
              before calling screener_getAltfinsScreenerData — use this tool to verify first
            - User wants to explore all available screener metrics before choosing which to use
    
            ### DO NOT USE THIS TOOL WHEN:
            - You already know the valid displayType or numericFilter values you need
              → call screener_getAltfinsScreenerData directly without discovery step
            - User wants actual screener results or coin data 
              → use screener_getAltfinsScreenerData instead
            - User wants analytics indicator types 
              → use analytics_getAnalyticsTypes instead (different set of types)
    
            ### RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER TOOLS:
            - This is a DISCOVERY tool for screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
            - The identifier values returned here are valid inputs for:
              - 'displayTypes' parameter in screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
              - 'numericFilterType' field within 'numericFilters' in screener_getAltfinsScreenerData
            - Typical workflow: call this tool once to discover valid identifiers,
              then use them in screener_getAltfinsScreenerData in the same session
    
            ### DIFFERENCE FROM analytics_getAnalyticsTypes:
            - This tool       → identifiers for screener_getAltfinsScreenerData filters/display
            - getAnalyticsTypes → identifiers for getHistoryAnalyticsData analyticsType param
            - These are DIFFERENT sets — do not mix them across tools
    
            ### IMPORTANT:
            - This tool takes no meaningful input — results are the same regardless of input
            - Results are static — the list of screener value types does not change between calls
            - No need to call this tool repeatedly in the same session

tools.name: technicalAnalysis_getTechnicalAnalysisData
tools.title: Technical Analysis
tools.description:
Returns a structured technical analysis summary including curated trade setups 
            for cryptocurrency assets, prepared by professional analysts on the altFINS platform.

            ### WHAT IS RETURNED:
            - Trade setup guidance with entry/exit context
            - Proprietary trend scoring (short, medium, long term)
            - Momentum assessment using MACD and RSI
            - Detection of major price patterns (triangles, wedges, channels, head & shoulders, etc.)
            - Identification of key support and resistance zones
            - Near-term outlook and pattern stage

            ### WHEN TO USE THIS TOOL:
            - User asks for "technical analysis", "trade setup", "chart analysis", or "price patterns"
            - User asks "is [coin] bullish or bearish?"
            - User asks "what is the outlook for [coin]?"
            - User wants a professional analyst view on a specific coin or the whole market

            ### COVERAGE:
            Curated setups exist only for the coins altFINS analysts cover, so for many symbols
            the result is empty or carries STATUS=NO_TRADE_SETUP_FOUND. That means no analyst
            setup exists for the symbol, not that altFINS has no data on it: the raw indicators
            for the same symbol are available from 'screener_getAltfinsScreenerData', with
            timeInterval=DAILY and displayTypes such as RSI14, MACD, SHORT_TERM_TREND,
            MEDIUM_TERM_TREND, SMA50, SUPPORT and RESISTANCE.

symbol.description:
Cryptocurrency symbol to retrieve technical analysis for.
            
                ### FORMAT:
                - Single symbol only, uppercase (e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL)
                - Leave empty or null to retrieve analysis for ALL available symbols
            
                ### EXAMPLES:
                - User asks "technical analysis for Bitcoin" → symbol=BTC
                - User asks "trade setup for Ethereum"      → symbol=ETH
                - User asks "show all trade setups"         → symbol=null
            
                ⚠️ Use uppercase ticker symbols only. Do not use full names (e.g. use BTC not Bitcoin).
                ⚠️ Do not pass multiple symbols here — call this tool once per symbol if needed.

page.description: Page number for pagination, zero-based index. Default is 0 (first page).

size.description:
Number of records per page. Default is 25. Maximum recommended is 50.
            
            💡 TIP: Use a lower value (10-20) for single symbol queries.
                Use a higher value (50) only when fetching all trade setups for a broad market overview.

sortField.description:
Field to sort results by.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES (use exact values, case-sensitive):
                - updatedDate    → sort by when the analysis was last updated (default)
                - symbol         → sort alphabetically by coin ticker
                - friendlyName   → sort alphabetically by coin full name
                - nearTermOutlook → sort by bullish/bearish outlook score
                - patternType    → sort by chart pattern type (e.g. triangle, wedge)
                - patternStage   → sort by how advanced the pattern is (early vs mature)
                - description    → sort by description text
                
                ### SELECTION GUIDE:
                - "most recently updated setups"     → updatedDate (default)
                - "most bullish setups"              → nearTermOutlook + sortDirection=DESC
                - "setups by pattern type"           → patternType
                - "most advanced/mature patterns"    → patternStage + sortDirection=DESC
                
                ⚠️ Only these exact values are accepted. Any other value will be ignored.

sortDirection.description:
Sort order direction.
            
                ### ALLOWED VALUES:
                - ASC  → ascending (oldest / lowest first)
                - DESC → descending (newest / highest first, default)
